claims.text: The menu centers on plain charcoal-grilled shellfish (turban shell, large clam, scallop, oyster), which is naturally wheat-free when prepared without soy sauce or batter.

name: ミュゼア コーヒー 鳥羽水族館店 (MUSEA COFFEE Toba Aquarium)

claims.text: The food menu centers on wheat-based bakery items (bread, bagels, scones, muffins, brownies, waffles, apple pie, paninis), so flour is handled throughout the small stand and cross-contact is likely.
Soft serve, baked goods, and milk-based drinks dominate the menu; no dairy-free or egg-free items are documented.
Cards are not accepted but electronic money and QR-code payments are, so a phone-based payment works.
Wheat-battered tempura (shrimp, spiny lobster) is on the menu and is fried in a shared kitchen; no dedicated fryer or allergen separation is mentioned.
Tekone sushi is bonito marinated in soy sauce, and Ise udon is served in a soy-based tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and the page gives no gluten-free soy alternative.
The menu centers on seafood with bonito-based dashi and tare; even noodle dishes use a fish-based sauce, so plant-only diners cannot rely on the standard preparations.

name: 御食事処 丸栄 (Oshokujidokoro Maruei)

claims.text: Multiple fried sets (shrimp, white fish, mixed fry) use wheat batter/breading and share fryer oil; no dedicated gluten-free fryer.

Entire menu is seafood and animal-based with fish/bonito dashi; no plant-based or vegetable-only dishes exist, so vegan dining is not feasible.
Wheat noodles (udon, ramen, soba) are the core of the menu and would share the same kitchen, boiling water, and prep surfaces — high cross-contamination risk for celiacs.
Standard Japanese shoyu and noodle broths (mentsuyu/dashi-based) used in udon, ramen, and teishoku here contain wheat; no gluten-free seasoning is indicated.
Broths and dashi are almost certainly fish/bonito-based, and the kitchen handles meat and fried foods throughout; assume animal cross-contact across the menu.

name: シーラウンジ S.Y.M (Sea Lounge S.Y.M)
